title: What If You Jumped on a Comet? You Might Never Come Down

scenes.text: What if you jumped on a comet? One hop could send you into space for good.
Comet 67P is about four kilometers across. Its gravity is roughly one ten-thousandth of Earth's.
Escape speed there is about half a meter per second, roughly one mile an hour. Slower than a stroll.
A normal walking push is faster than that, so you could leave the comet entirely.
Proof: in 2014 the Philae lander touched down at one meter per second and bounced up to about a kilometer high.
It stayed airborne for nearly two hours before landing again. On a comet, a hop is a launch.
